findings.reason: the constraint must say which entity's attempt the key is taken from (the node's last committed attempt, as the dispatch door already computes, or the run's) and require both doors to use that one source, or a resume and a dispatch racing on a run id that is not the node's newest committed run still both reserve and both launch.
findings.text: §13's "One holder, one key" names "the last committed attempt plus one" without saying whose last committed attempt: reckon/crew/dispatch.py:2704–2743 computes it over the node's committed runs (`prior_node_runs[-1]`, filtered by `node.id`, not by run id), so a run id that is not its node's newest committed run gets a different number than the run's own last committed attempt plus one — the number the resume door would derive from the record it holds (reckon/crew/resumption.py:405, `claim_next_attempt`) — and the two doors then hold reservations at different keys, each admitting its launch of the same run

response_events.note: §13 now keys every door on the run's own last committed attempt plus one, read by run id, not on the node's newest committed run, with a case relaunching a run that is not its node's newest.

reasoning-1.note: §13 now keys every door on the run's own last committed attempt plus one, read by run id, not on the node's newest committed run, with a case relaunching a run that is not its node's newest.
